submitted.rationale: Index 199 (Cr0.19 Fe0.70 V0.11) gave the highest photocurrent of the three measurements: 7.2e-7 A. Photocurrent went up as the film became more Fe-rich and lower in V: 7e-8 A near FeVO4, then 4.7e-7 A, then 7.2e-7 A. This suggests the best region is Cr-alloyed hematite with little V.

rejected.reason: Fe-rich but more V and less Cr than 199; 4.7e-7 A

consultations.verdict: MEGNet HSE gap for Fe2O3 (mp-19770) is 2.77 eV, which is above the 2.4 eV photon energy. That makes pure Fe-rich oxide a weak absorber here. FeVO4-type Fe:V≈1:1 phases usually have smaller gaps, around 2.0–2.1 eV. That supports measuring index 0 (Fe 0.41, V 0.49, low Cr), which is near FeVO4. Moderate support.

MEGNet HSE gap for mp-19399 is 2.38 eV, just under the 2.4 eV photon energy. Mixed Cr–Fe corundum oxides probably absorb at 2.4 eV. Index 0 (the FeVO4 region) gave only 7e-8 A, so I'm moving to the Fe-rich, low-V corner (index 60: Fe 0.73, Cr 0.11). There, Cr-alloyed hematite should narrow the gap. Weak support; this is mainly a test of a different region.

The SCAN-fidelity gap for mp-19399 (0.63 eV) disagrees sharply with the HSE value (2.38 eV), so it tells me nothing useful. My choice rests on the measured trend instead: the Fe-rich corner (4.7e-7 A) beat the FeVO4 region (7e-8 A). Index 199 has the least V among Fe-rich candidates (V 0.11, Fe 0.70, Cr 0.19), so it continues toward Cr–Fe oxide.
